notes: My guest today is Zach Reitano, the co-founder and CEO of Ro, the country’s leading provider of GLP-1s. In four years, Ro has grown from a $250 million run rate to over $3 billion, with fewer people than it had in 2021. The heart of our conversation is what he sees as the central flaw in American healthcare, which is that the patient is not the customer. He points to GLP-1s and LASIK as examples of what’s possible when patients pay directly, and he thinks AI could bring healthcare down to the price of a Netflix subscription. But to capture that opportunity, Zach first had to rebuild Ro's culture around high performance and a big heart. It shows in the stories Ro shares from people like Serena Williams, which help patients get past the stigma of seeking treatment. The inspiration behind it all is his father, a doctor whose care Zach wants to recreate in software. Please enjoy my conversation with Zach Reitano.  The Only Product Without Diminishing Returns 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Only Product Without Diminishing Returns 
 Patrick 
I've got a first question based on our last phone call, which was something you told me, which really stood out. What percent of GDP do you think healthcare could or should be ten, 15 years from now?

 Zach 
I think it should be as high as possible. 50, 70—

 Patrick 
Everyone's always complaining it's too high.

 Zach 
Everyone's always complaining it's too high. And I think that it's missing the forest for the trees. If you think about healthcare, I think it's the sine qua non of life. It's without which there is none. And it actually depends how AI-pilled you are, but your audience is probably pretty AI-pilled. But if you imagine a life of pure abundance and you imagine Jevons paradox does its thing, then the only good in our lives that does not have any diminishing marginal return is another healthy year. And so to me, at the limit, you should be spending every single dollar towards the health of your society.
